label: input h at the first or second original position
explanation: Token-and-position detector: fires only when the input token is h, and almost only at the start of the original phase (t = 0 or 1). Every dev activation has in_tok = h, and 99.5% of activation mass falls at t <= 1. Strength depends on position. At t = 0 it is maximal (1.727, the same value every time). At t = 1 it is weaker (about 0.6-0.8 of max), and the exact value depends on the preceding token (e.g. k gives 0.78, m 0.72, 3 0.66, z 0.62). At t = 2 there are weak, sparse residual activations (about 0.5% of mass), and when h repeats right after h the activation is near zero. It does not fire on h later in the original phase (t >= 3), on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (even when h is input or output there), and it never fires on any other token.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. Test: precision 1.0, recall 0.928, F1 0.963, mass recall 0.995, 0 false positives.

All test misses (2568 steps, 0.5% of mass) are h at t=2 with tiny activations (0.03-0.11 of max). Only 15% of h-at-t=2 steps fire (precision 0.153), so they are a weak, sparse tail and not a gap worth closing. h at t=2 right after h fires only 5.6% of the time, which supports the 'near zero when h repeats' claim.

The other claims check out on dev: 100% of activation mass is on in_tok=h; t=0 always gives the max value, 1.727 (1.00 relative); the delimiter never fires; the copy phase has 1 activation out of 2.7M steps, and t=4 has 1. h at t=1 right after h at t=0 still fires (precision 1.0), so the predicate holds there too.
Minor wording: 'it never fires on any other token' and 'no copy phase' are true up to single-step noise. 'Almost only at t=0 or 1' is accurate given the t=2 tail.
